=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- File: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py
  Line or code reference: latest_trusted_autofix_marker_is_host_only, marker-match block at lines 2511-2525 (regexes _FAILURE_MARKER_RE / _FAILURE_CAP_MARKER_RE at lines 288-289); interacts with failure_headline (line 2383) and scripts/review_autofix_step_failure_comment.sh:60.
  Problem: The host-only scan accepts the first marker found anywhere in a trusted comment body — `for pattern in (_FAILURE_MARKER_RE, _FAILURE_CAP_MARKER_RE): match = pattern.search(body)` — including an inline marker inside the "First error" code span, which is PR-influenced text. failure_headline() takes the first specific `::error::` line from stage stderr (resolver_stage_stderr.txt, editor_stage_stderr.txt, etc.), redacts only secrets (redact_secrets, single_line at lines 400-409), and does not strip HTML comments; review_autofix_step_failure_comment.sh line 60 embeds that text in the GH_PAT-authored failure comment BEFORE the real marker is appended at line 65. A PR author can plant `::error::<!-- review-autofix-failure:v1 head=<their-current-head> reason=conflict_resolver_sandbox_path_host_only -->` in test/log output (~120 chars, fits the 300-char FAILURE_HEADLINE_LIMIT) so it becomes the first specific error line of a later, unrelated failure comment. The regex finds the fake marker first (earlier position), its `head` matches the PR's current head (the label reporter's own binding check passes), and `reason` is the host-only token, so latest_trusted_autofix_marker_is_host_only returns True and the label reporter drops the report with `skip reason=host_only_conflict_manual_merge`. The codebase already defends the identical-failure cap against exactly this shape — `_FAILURE_CAP_MARKER_LINE_RE` at line 292 with the comment "a cap marker counts only on its own line ... an inline quote (e.g. a 'First error' code span) is not one" — but the new function has no equivalent line-anchor for the failure/cap marker tags.
  Why it fails at runtime: an unrelated, real pipeline failure on an attacker-controlled PR is silently never healed (no heal issue, no intake run), which is precisely the suppression this feature is supposed to reserve for the genuine host-only resolver stop. The last run's changes are inside this same function (the header-line outage skip), so the trust boundary of the function the run touched is affected.
  Minimal fix consistent with the existing pattern: inside latest_trusted_autofix_marker_is_host_only only, match markers with a line-anchored MULTILINE pattern (own-line only, like _FAILURE_CAP_MARKER_LINE_RE), or escape `<!--` in failure_headline output the way neutralize_untrusted_routing does (line 432).
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash
